limitations: P1 — Discounted optimality does not imply the claimed stabilization — Counterevidence: Five human experiments may remain successful; the witness is not a plant identification or an empirical harm claim.

P1 — Discounted optimality does not imply the claimed stabilization — Counterevidence: F.4's phrase 'updated by policy-gradient estimator' does not establish exact critic realization. The report deliberately limits the counterexample to the core idealized inference and does not claim every author-network training premise was executed.

P1 — Discounted optimality does not imply the claimed stabilization — Counterevidence: Page21's goal can be read as constrained to stabilizing policies, but Eqs17-20 use unrestricted pointwise action minimization and arbitrary initial policy. A stabilizing-policy admissibility restriction is an additional premise/algorithm change.

P1 — Discounted optimality does not imply the claimed stabilization — Counterevidence: Discounted costs can remain finite at nonzero equilibrium states. Stabilizability does not require every admissible or optimal policy to be stabilizing.

P1 — Discounted optimality does not imply the claimed stabilization — Counterevidence: Positive signs inEq14 can be a typo: released Adam code minimizes the losses. The sign alone is not separately graded.
